voice-branch-jargon.notes: No branch/audit working labels, bean ids, PR/branch references, audit-doc pointers, or agent work-narration found in the .md body or the .ts title.

trap-negation-contrast.evidence: 'This strictly differs from the structural GB-depth' is the block's disambiguating claim, stated positively as a difference between two named invariants.

trap-rhetorical-pivot.evidence: Two short paragraphs, five sentences; no reframe.

trap-triples.evidence: The title promises 'the THREE depth invariants' and the body distinguishes only TWO: the witness k_max (Coxeter-length filtration) and the structural GB-depth k_star(T_w). The only other symbol in the block, n_0, appears once as a bound (k_star <= n_0) and is never defined, so it does not supply a third invariant. Either the third was lost or the count is a reflex triple in the title.
trap-triples.notes: Proposed (structural — the fix requires knowing what the third invariant is): name and define the third depth invariant, or retitle to 'the two depth invariants'. Candidate for the missing third, from the sibling proof block: the empirical truncation level k = 2 (the 'subtractive sweet spot'), which is a third and genuinely distinct notion of depth.

trap-closing-aphorism.evidence: Closes on a technical requirement, not a quotable line.

trap-meta-commentary.evidence: no meta-commentary on the block's own rhetoric

trap-thesis-restatement.evidence: Paragraph 2 adds the bound and the Habiro requirement.

trap-superlative.evidence: 'strictly differs' and 'rigid upper bound' are mild; both attach to specific claims.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: Final sentence: 'The canonical real-valued mass requires the uniform z-Habiro bound to achieve canonical closed-form agreement, as truncation depths diverge empirically if left unregularized.' It uses 'canonical' twice as two different modifiers inside one sentence and ends on a subordinate clause; it stalls aloud.
trap-nonspeakable.notes: SUSPECTED SWEEP DAMAGE, reported for the coordinator rather than fixed (I could not confirm it from history — the file has a single commit, 230cdd113, so no earlier wording survives to diff against). The doubled 'canonical' fits the token-substitution class in which 'canonical' replaced 'numerical(ly)': read as 'The NUMERICAL real-valued mass requires the uniform z-Habiro bound to achieve NUMERICAL closed-form agreement', the sentence becomes coherent and matches the sibling proof block's framing ('its real-valued canonical evaluation at |V-hat| approx 1', 'the canonical mass formula at q = q_0'), where the same word sits where 'numerical' would be expected. Flagged at moderate confidence only: 'canonical' is also a live technical term in this corpus, so a reader who knows the intended sense should adjudicate before any sweep. Also unresolved: n_0 is used undefined.
